messages.subject: CANTAB gamble task model
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have been working through some of the models from this paper: ‘A computational model of the Cambridge gambling task with applications to substance use disorders’

https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0376871619304880#sec0070

I am unclear on the equations governing the bet valuation function from the supplementary material shown here:

For these models x is the cumulative total, so it is not possible for it be negative, in contrast to the text above. I interpreted x > 0 to mean a win and x < 0 to mean a loss in order to resolve this, but wanted to confirm that this is how the models were intended to be implemented?

Thanks,

Ani

messages.subject: Re: CANTAB gamble task model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ani,

Thanks for reaching out!

And yes, I see now that the notation is misleading in the supplement—your interpretation is correct. For the cumulative model, it is always the non-negative, cumulative total being evaluated. Which valuation function is used depends only on if the cumulative amount is decreasing (i.e. a "loss") or increasing (i.e. a "win").

Let me know if that is clear now, and thanks for the catch!

Best,
Nate

messages.subject: Question about coding outcomes in 2 arm bandit task
messages.subject_clean: Question about coding outcomes in 2 arm bandit task
messages.body_plain:
Dear colleagues,

First off, thanks very much for making the hBayesDM software package available!  I am very much enjoying utilizing it.

I have a simple two-arm bandit task that I'm attempting to model.  Each choice results in either a reward (25 cents) or no reward (0 cents).  There are no losses/punishments involved in this task.

My question is regarding the coding of the outcomes.  I notice in a prior message thread ("Fitting a probabilistic learning task with 4 stimuli") that it was stated by Nathaniel Haines that the outcomes should be coded as 1 and -1.  But if there are no losses involved, I'm having trouble understanding why the no gain outcome should be coded as -1?  Wouldn't the prediction error value then become larger than -1 on no reward trials but never larger than 1 on reward trials?  Is this desirable?

Thanks for your help!

Best,
Greg

messages.subject: Re: Question about coding outcomes in 2 arm bandit task
messages.subject_clean: Question about coding outcomes in 2 arm bandit task
messages.body_plain:
Hi Greg,

thanks for reaching out!

So in your case, it makes better sense to code outcomes as 1 (reward) and 0 (no reward). You may need to change the initial value in the model file (*.stan files), using 0.5 (averaged reward) instead of 0.

Hope that helps,
L.

messages.subject: two warnings from fitting the drift diffusion model
messages.subject_clean: two warnings from fitting the drift diffusion model
messages.body_plain:
Dear group,

I am fitting a drift diffusion model and I get two following warnings from Stan sampler in the initialization phase (both go away after a few warmup iterations):

1 - wiener_lpdf: Boundary separation is inf, but must be finite!
2 - wiener_lpdf: Random variable  = 0.327, but must be greater than nondecision time = 0.327. (other values appear as well.)

Is there a way to fix it? Is it kosher to ignore these? At the end, I get reasonable estimates after sampling, but these warning make me doubt my results.

Thank you so much!
